meter: USB power meter on the board's native USB port (display: V, A, mAh, Wh; read by eye)
method: each phase 600 s; energy = meter mAh x volts x 3.6 J; per inference = energy / runs; above idle = (mAh - idle mAh) x volts x 3.6 / runs; the meter counts whole mAh (+-1 mAh per reading); one run per phase; the board was slightly warm
tools: tools/energy_loop.py (firmware: 0xE5 loop on the last input, 'L:count,elapsed_us,class')

tflite.label: TFLite Micro INT8 (MLPerf ResNet-8, ESP-NN), flash

symbex.label: SYMBEX int8stem_pool2 seed 42, vertical engine (default), swar, flash

idle.label: idle: SYMBEX firmware waiting on the serial port

seeds_calculated.note: NOT measured: SYMBEX power of the seed-42 run x each seed's chip latency (same engine, same shape, same code)

prepared_vs_default.question: does spending RAM on prepared lists save energy, or only time? (reading more RAM could raise the power)

default.label: SYMBEX int8stem_pool2 seed 42, vertical engine (default), lut16, flash, 54 KB RAM; exact 100 %

prepared.label: SYMBEX int8stem_pool2 seed 42, vertical engine, prepared (lists and thresholds prepared in RAM), lut16, flash, 217 KB RAM; exact 100 %

notes: A first default run was not read in time: discarded and repeated.
The Nov 15 default run (24 mAh, 6.86 mJ) agrees with the Nov 14 one (25 mAh, 7.24 mJ, swar) within +-1 mAh.
prepared_vs_default.answer: it saves energy: 1.51x less per image (range 1.39-1.64) for 1.60x the speed; the prepared engine drew about 5 % more power (0.77 against 0.73 W), 1 mAh, at the meter's limit
